{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUhdMr88AAAABUhTPHg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlRslzg-Cjf8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlRsl", "number": 110, "title": "Guide Issue authors to avoid unnecessary human-dependent acceptance criteria", "body": "## Problem

Issue acceptance criteria can inadvertently require work that an AI agent cannot perform autonomously, such as a human checking a physical mobile device. Such criteria should be mandatory only when they are necessary. Otherwise, a small implementation task can become blocked on an unnecessary human check.

For example, takahirox/my-audio-to-text#15 included verifying that its published URL could be opened from a mobile browser. When the remaining validation work was split into #17, the new Issue required an actual mobile browser, device/browser/result evidence, and explicitly rejected viewport emulation. This introduced a mandatory physical-device check into an AI-driven task. The intended principle is not to prohibit human validation, but to make its necessity and expected result explicit.

GitWeave's development guidance and Issue template are used as references by other repositories. They currently describe the problem/outcome/context structure but do not explain how to choose acceptance criteria suitable for AI-assisted work.

## Expected outcome

Add concise guidance in two existing locations:

- `docs/development-flow.md`, under “1. Start with an Issue”: explain the policy.
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md`, under “Expected outcome”: add a short authoring reminder and a link to the development guidance.

Proposed wording for the guidance:

> By default, completion criteria should be executable and verifiable by an AI agent. Require human checks, such as physical-device testing, subjective evaluation, or external approval, only when there is a necessary reason to do so.
>
> When human work is required, state why it is necessary and what result is expected. Distinguish optional additional validation from mandatory completion criteria.

Keep the template small and the guidance proportionate to the existing document. Human validation remains allowed when necessary; this is not permission to drop genuinely required checks or to claim unperformed tests passed.

Do not add a requirement to name an assignee or human tester. Do not add a separate policy about preserving requirements during Issue splitting or updates; those are intentionally outside this wording change. Wait/resume behavior, PR closing directives, and runtime changes are also outside this Issue.

Completion means the development guidance contains the policy, the Issue template has the concise reminder and working guidance link, and the repository artifacts are written in English. Existing templates copied into other repositories do not update automatically; propagating the wording elsewhere is separate work.

## Context

- Development guidance: https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md
- Issue template: https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md
- Original deployment Issue: https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/15
- Follow-up validation Issue: https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/17

The agreed wording focuses on avoiding unnecessary human-dependent completion criteria and clarifying necessary human checks. It does not require CI, bots, new workflow fields, or a broader process framework.
